speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Although smoking rates have dipped from a high of 23% in 1977 to 12% today, its associated diseases continue to claim the lives of more than 2,000 Singaporeans each year, or an average of six persons every day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The health effects from exposure to second-hand smoke are also well-documented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: To tackle tobacco addiction, the Government adopts a comprehensive, multi-pronged approach which involves curtailing access to cigarettes, sustaining public education and cessation efforts, and restricting where one can smoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We have been a global frontrunner in tobacco control and were one of the first countries to prohibit smoking in public places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Today, curbs on tobacco advertising and a minimum legal age for smoking are in force, and more than 32,000 places have been made smoke-free.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Our vision is to become a smoke-free nation where tobacco use is discouraged, and people can enjoy clean air and a conducive living environment, free from passive smoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will continue to press on towards this goal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Last year, we announced plans to turn the Orchard Road precinct into a "No-Smoking Zone" (NSZ).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The shopping belt was chosen because of the heavy footfall it experiences year-round, both from locals and tourists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: As a destination attraction, Orchard Road draws large crowds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We want to ensure that pedestrians, particularly families with young children and elderly, are protected from passive tobacco smoke along the busy thoroughfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Many businesses operating in the NSZ have expressed support for this initiative, which is in line with their plans to ramp up new offerings and activities along the shopping belt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: My thanks go out to the Orchard Road Business Association (ORBA) in particular for facilitating the preparations for the NSZ.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: But the journey to quit smoking is a challenging one, and smokers need time to wean themselves off the habit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We recognise this and will make provisions for smoking at certain designated areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This pragmatic approach maintains a balance between the interests of smokers and non-smokers, even as we discourage tobacco consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Once designated an NSZ, every publicly accessible place within the NSZ will become smoking-prohibited, including along uncovered footpaths and pedestrian crossings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: It will be an offence to smoke at these places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The existing smoking-prohibited places, such as the shopping malls and the common areas of commercial office buildings, will remain smoke-free.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The penalty for unlawful smoking within an NSZ will be no different from that imposed in any other smoking-prohibited place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Under the new section 3C, it will be made clear that managers of premises may set up designated smoking areas (DSAs) within their compounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These facilities must conform to prescribed requirements in respect of their design, amenities and location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For example, DSAs must not be located in certain types of smoking-prohibited places and must not obstruct public walkways and cause disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will periodically review the requirements to guard against a proliferation of DSAs and ensure that these facilities serve their purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Ahead of the establishment of the Orchard Road NSZ, businesses and premises owners have worked with NEA to identify suitable locations for DSAs, away from the main thoroughfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The various DSAs are spaced out for convenient access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: When the NSZ is in operation, Singaporeans and tourists can look forward to cleaner air along Orchard Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Under the existing Act, the managers of smoking prohibited places are responsible for ensuring the ban is observed within their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The vast majority do so, including those managing coffee shops and food courts, and I appreciate their efforts in safeguarding a smoke-free environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, from time to time, there is a minority who disregard their responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA has faced challenges in investigating complaints about smoking violations at smoking-prohibited places where access is restricted, particularly in public entertainment outlets, such as nightclubs and pubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Currently, to investigate complaints about smoking violations, NEA enters and inspects the premises with the manager’s consent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While most have been cooperative, some managers have hindered investigations by denying NEA’s authorised officers entry into their premises, which prevents timely, effective investigation and enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We are, therefore, introducing new sections 4A and 4B to explicitly provide NEA's authorised officers the powers to enter, without warrants, smoking-prohibited places to investigate feedback on related infractions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For all other smoking-prohibited places, NEA can invoke the power of entry at all reasonable times, such as the operating hours of the place, or at any time if there is reasonable belief that an offence under the Act has been committed there, or that evidence of an offence can be found there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: It will also become an offence to obstruct, hinder or delay authorised officers exercising these powers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA’s authorised officers enforcing the smoking ban at times encounter belligerent smokers who turn aggressive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The provisions in section 4B will explicitly make it an offence to obstruct, hinder or delay these authorised officers in the performance of their duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Those who verbally or physically abuse an authorised officer will also be liable under these provisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Penalties will likewise be levied on those who furnish false or misleading information, including those who withhold identification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These amendments aim to deter uncooperative smokers from hindering the agency’s enforcement efforts and underscore our firm stance against abusive and uncivil behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Similar offences can be found in other laws, such as the Environmental Public Health Act and the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will ensure that only authorised personnel, such as NEA officers involved directly in the investigations, would have access to evidence collected during investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The remaining clauses 5 to 8 in the Bill are technical in nature and are made for clarity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The proposals in this Bill serve to discourage smoking and enable us to protect more Singaporeans against second-hand smoke exposure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Nonetheless, smoking is likely to continue in Singapore and around the world for some time to come and we must take a practical approach towards regulating smoking activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Our smoke-free vision is a work in progress and we will continue to press on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While enforcement measures are being augmented, the efforts of the community remain key to fostering considerate behaviour amongst smokers and nudging them towards kicking the habit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I, therefore, seek Members’ support for this Bill.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Way back in 1986, posters already warned that smoking causes lung cancer and heart attacks.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, as more research and statistics about the health risks of smoking and second-hand smoke surfaced, public awareness campaigns all over the world have also become increasingly graphic and aggressive.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Nevertheless, the effect is limited, especially on those who have already picked up the habit.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For those of us who have friends and family members who smoke, many of them are kind enough to walk away when they need a puff.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They clearly understand the effects of smoking, and they do not wish to cause harm to their loved ones, yet they are doing this to themselves.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is the battle against cigarette addiction that forms the backdrop to what we discuss today.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are several aspects of the Bill I welcome wholeheartedly and several places it can go further.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The increased powers to manage prohibited smoking spots is, hopefully, an indication that there are further plans to implement smoking prohibition in more places, not just in Orchard Road.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased that the Bill takes into consideration the welfare of our NEA officers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Certainly, uncooperative offenders who abuse our officers deserve to be apprehended.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, even if we enhance enforcement powers and prohibit smoking in more places, it is pointless if people continue to light up where they should not if they believe they can get away with it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Lack of enforcement continues to be a problem that undermines the effectiveness of this policy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is a difficult task to catch a smoker red-handed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Most people do not smoke beyond a few minutes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, even if a report is made, by the time an NEA officer comes, the smoker would have left.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Most people are afraid to take front-view pictures of smokers because it may escalate into a conflict.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, requesting for pictorial evidence of illegal smoking, too, has its limitations.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And, despite the numerous closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras installed in public areas, these devices are meant to monitor and deter crimes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is even happening in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, where the offender is a resident.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Despite numerous reports from other affected residents, the NEA officers are unable to book the offender red-handed, so the smoker continues to get away scot-free.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the authorities will address the difficulties of catching and penalising smoking at prohibited areas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Everyone deserves the freedom to do what he or she likes in their own homes, as long as we do not break the law or harm anyone.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, the question we need to ask is: does smoking in one’s own house cause harm or is injurious to anyone’s health?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When they smoke in the presence of family members, especially young children, without a doubt, the answer is yes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When the smoke drifts out of the window and infiltrates a neighbour’s house, that is another definite yes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Like all addictions, once smoking takes root, it is challenging to be smoke-free.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: One can argue that if other countries cannot do it, why should we be so “kia-su” and so "kia-si"?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We can rest on our laurels and wait for someone to work out a solution and then we adapt it for our own use.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But no, we are Singapore, a small nation capable of accomplishing lofty ambitions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We eradicated opium smoking, despite one in four Chinese adults being addicted to opium in 1933.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Undesirable and common habits like spitting and vandalism by way of chewing gum are shadows of the past.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am confident that we can eradicate smoking that affects neighbours if the authorities are firm about it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We can start with a gradual approach by rationing the amount of sales and drastically increasing taxes on cigarettes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We can channel the extra taxes back into programmes that help people quit smoking.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need not ban the act of smoking itself, but we can make cigarettes much less available.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In the interim, more support and assistance must be available for smokers across all demographics to help them kick the habit, if they wish to.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, in raising the legal smoking age, some young smokers who have been smoking illegally may be afraid to come forward to seek help, so this is something to consider.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, we need to strengthen education on the ills of smoking in primary schools and secondary schools.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin): This Bill will allow the Government to set up more designated smoking areas and better protect the NEA officers who are enforcing the law.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, even with these regulations, smokers can still light up at smoking-prohibited areas and get away with it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is because many people are afraid to take a front shot of the smoker's face and the enforcement officers may not be able to reach there before the smoker stubs out.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government can explore how to address these enforcement challenges.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is more, many people smoke in their own homes, posing a risk to their family members, especially the children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It will also affect the living environment of the neighbours.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, there have been many conflicts caused by this problem.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is also something that the Government should look into.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But compared to the harm done by smoking and second-hand smoking to people's health, they are worthy of our serious consideration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that NEA’s goal is to move the policy from a prohibitive list to a positive list, which states places where smoking is allowed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill is a step in that direction and I stand in full support of it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a former smoker who smoked for 17 years, I am passionate about fighting against the dangers of smoking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a father, I am now doing all I can to protect my three daughters against the harmful effects of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Those who are exposed to second-hand smoke face similar health risks as a smoker.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These include eye, nose and throat irritations, respiratory tract infections, heart disease and cancer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Children and pregnant women are particularly susceptible to the effects of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, children of smokers are more likely to pick up smoking themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are now doing a lot to protect people from second-hand smoke in public areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the concern which Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has just mentioned is that what has been raised also previously in this House is: what are we doing to protect people from second-hand smoke in their own homes?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would seem at odds to protect people from second-hand smoke in the public areas where they spend less time and not protect them at home where they spend more time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of my residents complain about being affected by second-hand smoke when their neighbours smoke at their windows or balconies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As HDB units are close to one another, what happens next door inadvertently affects neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For those who live next to, or above, chain smokers, the problem can be very acute.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine being exposed to and having to tolerate second-hand smoke from your neighbours every day for years with the only reprieve being moving out altogether.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is the reality faced by some of my residents, which I am sure is shared by many others.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the Act currently covers smoking in private vehicles in cases where windows are not fully wound up and smoke is expelled into smoking prohibited places.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that it also covers any area within five metres of windows, exits and entrances to buildings where smoking is prohibited.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These restrictions are based on the logic that cigarette smoke can be expelled up to five metres away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, applying the same logic, can the law be extended to prohibit smoking in private homes where the smoker is smoking at a window or door within five metres of their neighbour’s windows and doors?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But my hope is that the Ministry would study this issue further, do a public consultation about it and try to find a middle ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that the Senior Minister of State's reply will be what she said previously, that “Smoking within residential premises, in the home, in private space, is beyond the jurisdiction of the Government.” But we do have regulations that cover what you do in your home, in your own private space.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, we have regulations that prohibit making excessive noise in your own house.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have regulations saying you cannot be naked in your own house.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under section 27A of the Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act, a person cannot be naked in a private space while being exposed to public view.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also want to add that it was reported just last month that the United States (US) implemented a ban on smoking inside public housing to improve indoor air quality, to reduce residents’ exposure to second-hand smoke, and to help smokers to be more successful at quitting.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Sir, in a Facebook comment, Mr Loh shared with me the very common experience of pedestrians forced to breathe in second-hand smoke when they walk behind smokers who smoke while on the move.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: New York City is now also considering a Bill that would similarly prohibit people from smoking while walking on sidewalks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the Ministry consider a ban on smoking while walking, which would stamp out the unpleasant situation highlighted by Mr Loh that many of us have faced?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such a ban could be piloted on major streets with heavy pedestrian footfall, such as those in the Central Business District and the Civic District.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, earlier this year, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor shared that the Ministry is exploring the feasibility of expanding the designated smoking area scheme first implemented in Orchard Road to other parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned this in her opening speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry provide more updates on this review and share if there are plans to scale up the scheme?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I also ask what would be the guidelines used in determining the suitability of locating a smoking facility under section 3B?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I raise this as in some of the current eateries where there is a designated smoking area, it really does not matter where you sit as you will get the second-hand smoke whether you are in the designated smoking area or not.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, I refer to the new section 4A which provides authorised officers with certain powers of entry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, these powers may be exercised by non-uniformed public officers, as with many of the other Bills passed recently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the need to empower non-uniformed public officers, in this case NEA officers, to help with enforcement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a firm step towards our vision of a smoke-free lifestyle in Singapore.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I support the move on the general expansion of places to be prescribed as specific places with the intent to have more smoke-free public areas, in line with the overall goal of discouraging smoking among the population and with the hope that such restrictions will protect the rights of non-smokers to breathe in clean air, that is, smoke-free air, and for smokers to gradually reduce smoking and eventually give up the habit.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Smoke-free areas will help reduce a non-smoker’s exposure to harmful second-hand cigarette smoke.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, the onus must be on the operators and premises managers to stop patrons, visitors, customers and staff from smoking in such prohibited areas or request that they leave the premises, which may affect their businesses.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: There must be public education to encourage and empower non-smokers to step up by reminding smokers not to light up in smoking prohibited areas.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: There are also concerns that if the community were to be bold enough to do so, they can inevitably be abused by the smokers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, it is important that we also educate our smokers to smoke responsibly with the community in mind and to do so in smoking areas only.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Many conscious non-smokers are of the view that having a designated smoking facility is, indeed, a compromise by the authority and that the Government should work towards removing such provision completely in the long term.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In anticipation of backlash among some segments of the population, there is also a need to explain the caveat that comes with the no-smoking zone within the prohibited areas, that there will be designated areas where smoking is still permitted.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: A generic concern would be, when we prohibit the sales of a commodity, there will be a likelihood of a black market.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Applying the same concept, by further restricting the areas that people can smoke, are we inevitably creating “black zones”?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: How can we ensure a good balance of prohibition, regulation and enforcement to ensure that smokers comply with the regulations without having to dramatically increase enforcement officer presence?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If we are very serious about making the large part of Singapore a smoke-free city, can we make use of the latest technology, predictive analytical programmes as well as AI, to identify violations and potential violations by smokers as well as errant operators?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This would also serve to help us with our endeavour to be environmentally friendly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the amendments to increase the number of places where smoking is banned and to entrust our enforcement officers with additional powers, I am confident we will see further progress in our fight against the scourge of smoking.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In popular and crowded places, such as the Orchard Road shopping belt, legislation to designate all public areas within it as part of an NSZ will allow everyone, young and old, to enjoy cleaner air free from pollution.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are designated smoking areas in an NSZ which will provide them with an outlet.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additional powers of entry, taking photographs and videos will enable our officers to carry out their duties more effectively and are necessary to conduct proper investigations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also want to share this picture from The Straits Times in case Members missed it after the National Day Rally.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is a very interesting one after the Prime Minister had mentioned Home Improvement Programme II (HIP II), the wish list from residents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, the wish list is whether they can have a fan to blow the harmful second-hand smoke back into the smoker's face.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That is the wish list for HIP II.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For years, non-smokers have been complaining about neighbours smoking at their window ledges, along common corridors and at landings between staircases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think this is a common issue that all of us faced as Members of Parliament during the Meet-the-People sessions.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The resultant air pollution not only causes discomfort, for residents with health problems, the smoke can even trigger an asthma attack.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Families with vulnerable young children and elderly members are particularly concerned.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Non-smokers also complained about smoking at coffee shops and inconsiderate smokers smoking in the public lifts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Smoking is one of the main causes of friction in our community and disputes among neighbours, as pointed out by Members earlier on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin): Unfortunately, despite public knowledge about the harmful effects of smoking and the additional problems created by second-hand and third-hand smoke, the number of smokers in our midst have not gone down as much as we would like.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They ask for understanding from non-smokers and protest the deprivation of their spaces of freedom and enjoyment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the other hand, non-smokers are calling for a total ban.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can consider effective measures and best practices in other countries to strike a balance between the two groups, for example, setting up smoking rooms with air filters or purification machines in public facilities, office buildings and shopping malls.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, we must persist in continuing our public education to let our citizens understand the harm of smoking more deeply.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have to pay special attention to our younger generation to prevent them from picking up the bad habit of smoking or follow in the footsteps of older smokers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that some smokers, influenced by our environment, will see the light sooner or later, and once they understand, they will naturally be determined to abandon this bad habit which is harmful to others and themselves.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I have long been concerned about the dangerous effects of smoking and thus strongly support the amendments to the Bill which I hope will help to reduce the prevalence of smoking.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Tobacco is a slow and silent killer with an extensive reach.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Its fumes blight all who inhale, including unwilling victims through second-hand smoke.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Its menace lingers in a vicinity long after the smoker has left, through third-hand smoke which clings to surfaces, posing a health hazard to anyone exposed to it.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope, in future, we can go even further by turning our entire island into a smoke-free zone where smokers could only smoke in designated smoking areas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Clean, unpolluted air is a precious resource which is everyone’s right.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Yet, despite awareness about smoking’s impact on health, a significant number of Singaporeans and residents cannot get rid of their nicotine addiction.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Their smoking habit caused much discomfort to those around them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many residents complain to me about neighbours who smoke.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Smoke spreads out of the smokers’ windows and pollutes neighbouring homes and the public corridors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Smoking in stairwells and elevators are also a problem.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In coffee shops, the fumes from the smokers who sit in the outdoor area blow into the indoor dining area.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The cigarette butts are not only dirty and unsanitary, they pose a fire hazard.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Anyone who wants to smoke in their homes must ensure that their cigarette smoke does not escape from their apartments and flats to pollute the environment outside their homes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In other words, windows and doors should be closed when smoking.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Smokers may consider installing an air filter in their rooms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They should not be standing near the windows, doors or corridors to smoke.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As a first step, neighbours should try to persuade the neighbours who are smoking to smoke in a more considerate way, either by talking to them directly or through relevant agencies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If it does not work, then they may ask the enforcement officers to step in.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another suggestion is to set up a smoking room in a coffee shop near a walkway that is not frequently used.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents complain that on the way to the Mass Rapid Transit station, shops or clinic, they have to hold their breath when passing by coffee shops.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Setting up smoking rooms in these coffee shops is a win-win solution, allowing smokers and non-smokers to co-exist in harmony.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: While it may still be a long while before we become a smoke-free society, it is a step forward when we broaden the scope to have more designated NSZs and enhancing the responsibilities as well as enforcement that can be carried out by specific appointed groups beyond the agencies.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Second-hand smoke is known to pose health hazards and researchers have shown that it does contain the same harmful chemicals that smokers inhale.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There is just no safe level of exposure for second-hand smoke and it is known to cause cancer, apart from other health issues.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Why then does this become a social issue?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Simply because this is a topic beyond personal choices but rather it encompasses infringement of the rights of others.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For the young children and those who are non-smokers, they surely have a right of not being constantly exposed to second-hand smoke.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Both incidents were during my house visits at different locations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I recalled the first incident was when I was walking down a common corridor at one of the HDB flats.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The distinct smell of tobacco was lingering in the air.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As I was entering one of the flats, that smell was clearly overpowering over that unit.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For a moment, I thought there must be some heavy chain smoker living in that unit.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The lady owner, a mother of two young children, actually pointed out to me, and had an aggrieved look, when she said this.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: She said that she had to seal up all the front windows facing the common corridor, shut her main door and turn on the air-conditioning for many hours each day whenever her preschoolers were at home.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: She simply had no choice as several members of her immediate neighbouring units are chain smokers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The crux of the issue was that her neighbours would not be smoking within their units and preferred to do so along the common corridor or even at the common staircase.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: At another block of flats, other residents raised similar concerns but, this time, it is about smoking at the stairwell and by non-residents.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They have identified some of these smokers as underaged youths, and others were tenants who lived in the rental flats.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The secondary issue that resulted from their smoking is the random littering of cigarette butts at the stairwell and parapets.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Now, the question becomes one of fairness and enforcement.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Do the others who are non-smokers have to bear with the inconsiderate actions of the smokers and do the cleaners have to suffer from picking up after the smokers?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With this context in mind and for better understanding of how the amendments will subsequently be instituted, I would like to seek several clarifications from the Minister.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Can the Minister share the guidelines of how this will be decided?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Three, for residential estates, are we likely to see an increase of designated smoking facilities and what are the guidelines for a smoking facility to be considered complying to acceptable standards?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As these individuals are likely to be the managing agent or volunteers of the Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST), what enforcement powers will be conferred to the individual who is carrying out his or her duties in order to protect them?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Lastly, for implementation of the Bill within the private condominiums after it is enacted, is there a requirement for the MCST to gain consensus and pass a resolution for this addition to their by-laws before a specific room or place within their compound can be designated as a NSZ?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In cases where the MCST is unable to gain majority consensus for the resolution, what recourse can members supportive of the Act have?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As reflected in the clarifications that I sought, implementation will be critical when the Bill is passed.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Only time will tell how much effect the Bill will bring about, how smokers and non-smokers can live within the shared spaces, and what pressure will society impress upon smokers as the general population becomes aware of the harmful effects to health.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Nevertheless, I look forward to the implementation of the Bill as it will bring about the necessary changes that impact others on a topic which is not one of preference, but a changing social attitude in our country.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is clearly not good news to all the smokers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But for the majority who crave for clean air wherever they go, the national effort in creating and promoting a smoke-free lifestyle in Singapore is a welcome one.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This issue, which had been discussed in Parliament before, was also raised by my colleagues earlier.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Smoking within residential homes is understandably not prohibited.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In fact, with all the extension of smoke-free areas, the home is probably one of the few spaces left for the smoker to smoke in peace.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, the problem occurs when the resident smokes while standing at his or her window or balcony.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The smoke, and often the ash, travel to his or her neighbours’ homes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This causes much grievance to other residents in the block.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I recall that one of my residents who complained about this issue lamented that it is ironical that with so much regulation to create a smoke-free environment in public spaces, he and his family members are unable to enjoy a smoke-free environment in their own homes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: On one occasion, I received a poignant plea from a resident living in a condominium.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He is a lung cancer survivor and is naturally concerned about breathing in passive smoke.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: His neighbour, however, has a habit of smoking at his window.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, this resident had to constantly close his windows and stuff a cloth at the bottom of his main door, just so that the smoke does not travel into his unit.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He begged for the managing agent, MSCT and NEA to intervene.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There was little that could be done, save for advising and encouraging the neighbour to stop smoking from the window.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The situation improved after some time but would recur once in a while.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: My grassroots leaders and the managing agent would try their best to assist to address the feedback whenever it is raised.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But this is clearly not the most ideal resolution of the matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The second issue that I would like to highlight is the lack of cooperation of smokers in the absence of enforcement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: From the feedback that I have received on the ground, smokers do not appear to comply with the rules and can be quite defiant when reminded by others not to smoke in certain places.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some can be seen smoking in the parks within the housing estates and, when told not to do so by passers-by, will arrogantly state that there is no one around to issue them the summons.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have received this feedback from many residents and friends.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Related to this point, there seems to be a lack of understanding about the rules relating to smoking in sheltered walkways or drop-off points.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some smokers seem to think that when it rains, it is unreasonable to disallow them to smoke in covered spaces when it is raining.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have received feedback from people who see smokers at sheltered walkways during the rain and also appeals from those who feel that they should not be penalised if they were caught smoking while seeking refuge from the rain.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I note the efforts in recruiting volunteer enforcement officers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If not, what are the efforts to build on this capacity?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Has the current effort in tapping on volunteers been successful?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand that this is extremely difficult to control and there are various views on the matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are residents who feel strongly that there should not be regulation that impinges on what they can or cannot do at home.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, I feel that what needs to be emphasised is the adverse impact on others.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand that the matter is not quite straightforward.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, the enforcement of this would require evidence which may be tricky to obtain.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I feel though, if someone repeatedly commits the offence, it would be possible to track the unit from which the smoke comes from and issue a notice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I also feel that the enforcement approach could be in phases, with the issuance of a warning first.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In any case, the legislation would send a strong message about the seriousness of the matter and deter residents from smoking at the windows or balconies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At the end of the day, I feel that public education is the most important in encouraging people to embrace the importance and value of a smoke-free environment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I truly appreciate the current efforts already in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One message we could amplify is the impact of smoking on others.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Smokers do not appear to appreciate the value of the rules in place but are, rather, only triggered by the fear of enforcement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The softer and tandem approach of educating and supporting them to quit smoking should be enhanced and amplified to reach out to more.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand that there are many challenges, and I truly appreciate the effort and multiple approaches taken by the Ministry and NEA in tackling the issue.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members have voiced concerns about the harm posed by passive cigarette smoke to vulnerable groups, such as the young and the elderly, and asked what more can be done.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some, including Miss Cheryl Chan, have also asked whether more NSZs are being planned.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We decided on the shopping belt because the area experiences significant and dense pedestrian traffic and is a site for alfresco activities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We had strong backing for our plans from businesses and building owners, led by the Orchard Road Business Association.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also considered the availability of suitable locations for Designated Smoking Areas (DSAs), given that the NSZ would cover a relatively large area with numerous commercial premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since 2015, NEA has been working with building owners in Orchard Road to allocate sufficient space for DSAs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As far as possible, these DSAs are located away from the main thoroughfare along Orchard Road, to ensure smoking is contained and not done in clear view of passers-by, especially impressionable youths.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will help protect public health and avoid normalising smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Like Ms K Thanaletchimi, I hope that DSAs would become unnecessary one day.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we must be practical in our approach, given the large number of visitors and tourists along Orchard Road.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng suggested a pilot to prohibit smoking while on the move.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Outside of the NSZ, smoking is already disallowed in many public places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This includes sheltered pedestrian walkways, overhead bridges and the corridors of public estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our priority is to implement the NSZ well, monitor the outcomes and make any necessary improvements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will then assess the impact of the Orchard Road NSZ and its DSAs, before considering whether to replicate it elsewhere.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng and Miss Cheryl Chan asked if we plan to provide DSAs in places beyond Orchard Road, such as in our housing estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Unlike Orchard Road, our heartlands are where our homes and schools are, and where our young children and youths spend their time daily.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: DSAs typically serve as congregation points for smokers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The daily sight of people gathering to smoke at DSAs at residential areas may give our young the impression that it is normal to smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As much as possible, we want to avoid this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Furthermore, given the design of our housing estates where HDB blocks are well-connected and dense, it may be challenging to find suitable locations that ensure that DSAs are not too conspicuous.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, our approach has instead been to extend the smoking prohibition to as many areas as possible within housing estates where members of the public frequent, including sheltered walkways, exercise areas and playgrounds.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor and enforce against smoking violations in these areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members have also called for restrictions on smoking in homes, including imposing penalties when smoke wafts out of a residential unit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, indiscriminate smoking can be distressing, and I empathise with all those who are affected.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to be mindful that not everyone would support the view that the Government should intrude into one’s private space on the issue of smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, the Member Ms Rahayu Mahzam had alluded to that earlier.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have witnessed disputes in some private estates over the management committee’s right to prohibit smoking in one’s balcony – a private space.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Mr Louis Ng rightly pointed out, regulation must be balanced against privacy concerns.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Moreover, if we were to prohibit smoking in one’s own home, it would inevitably entail bringing to bear the necessary investigation and enforcement powers in our homes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Such an intrusive regulatory approach to tackling neighbourly issues could ultimately be even more detrimental to community harmony and ownership.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng cited a recent US ban on smoking within public housing estates as an example of how a comparable regime could be implemented in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The US smoking ban does not apply to all homes, but only to public housing estate for low-income residents, through the imposition of conditions in the tenancy agreements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Tenants who do not wish to comply with the smoking ban may have to look for alternative housing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The context of the US smoking ban is very different, and we do need to consider our local circumstances before adopting practices from abroad.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have been proactively addressing second-hand smoke in our housing estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the years, we have disallowed smoking at common areas, including at the lift lobbies, corridors and staircase landings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In response to Ms Rahayu Mahzam’s comment that there is a lack of understanding about the rules relating to smoking in sheltered walkways or drop-off points, especially during rain, we would like to clarify that the smoking prohibition applies regardless of the weather.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ultimately, living in the community is about give and take.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I urge all smokers to be considerate and to refrain from smoking in a way that would negatively affect others.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Families and friends of the smokers as well as the public, in general, could help to reinforce the right social norms, through nudges and reminders, in order to help address this issue.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the spirit of good neighbourliness, we should try to understand one another’s concerns, communicate and resolve disputes amicably.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If professional assistance is required, residents can approach the Community Mediation Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Rahayu Mahzam highlighted the frustrations of non-smokers faced with inconsiderate smokers around their neighbourhood.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They have asked about enforcement capacity, and how we plan to make enforcement more effective and efficient in light of the growing number of smoke-free places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Enforcement is necessary, but not the silver bullet.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Instead, our deeper aim is to foster social norms that promote health and well-being.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need the community to help us remind smokers where they should not be smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smokers must also play their part and be mindful of those around them before lighting up.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked how technology can be further leveraged to facilitate reporting of unlawful smoking and errant managers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members of the public can notify NEA about smoking violations through the myENV and OneService mobile applications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These cameras are equipped with heat-detection capabilities that can detect smoking activity and can be operated remotely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When deployed, these cameras will be able to capture images of the smoking infringement and facilitate NEA’s investigations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In response to Ms Rahayu Mahzam’s question whether the Community Volunteer (CV) programme has enhanced enforcement of the smoking prohibition, let me clarify that CVs are not deployed to supplement NEA’s enforcement officers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The CVs’ primary role is to educate environmental offenders and promote environmental consciousness in the community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: CVs can only ask for the particulars of uncooperative offenders and can give the information to NEA for investigation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: CVs have been deployed in Orchard Road to raise awareness of the upcoming NSZ and help ease smokers into the regime when it comes into operation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These efforts should also go some way in minimising smoking violations within the newly prohibited places, a concern raised by Ms Thanaletchimi.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We should adopt a whole-of-society approach towards encouraging gracious behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This way, we can all enjoy clean air in the shared spaces around us, while building a stronger community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I agree with Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Thanaletchimi that public education is a critical plank in our efforts to create a smoke-free environment, and we will explore ways to further enhance that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Beyond encouraging smokers to be considerate, we also want to help them quit smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) will expand its outreach and support network through its "I Quit" campaign.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The campaign will raise awareness about the harms of smoking and encourage smokers to kick the habit for the sake of their families.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Joan Pereira suggested providing smoking rooms in premises, such as office buildings, public facilities and coffee shops.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While smoking rooms may reduce exposure to second-hand tobacco smoke, they cannot eliminate it completely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The smoke can still seep into other parts of the building where people do not smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, we have restricted where and how smoking rooms can be set up.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smoking rooms are only allowed in certain premises, such as office buildings and public entertainment outlets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, the smoking room has to meet requirements, such as having separate ventilation and must not be used by any employee for work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng and Miss Cheryl Chan asked about the guidelines for smoking facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Within the Orchard Road NSZ, a DSA must be demarcated clearly and be provided with at least one cigarette waste bin.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The DSA must not be located where smoking is currently prohibited and must not obstruct public walkways or cause disamenities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: An example of a DSA that complies with these requirements is the one located at Far East Shopping Centre currently.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There, the DSA is inconspicuously located at a distance from the pedestrian thoroughfare and in the open, so second-hand smoke does not accumulate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms K Thanaletchimi asked that time be given to managers who are required to set up smoking facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will give sufficient notice to the manager of a place to set up any DSA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, businesses and premises owners have worked with NEA to identify suitable locations for DSAs since 2017, ahead of the establishment of the Orchard Road NSZ.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Existing food establishments that change hands and are issued a new licence would similarly have to remove their smoking corners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have taken these steps to increasingly create a smoke-free dining experience for everyone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the rationale for the provisions on enforcement powers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I mentioned earlier, NEA has, at times, encountered challenges in investigating complaints about smoking in certain smoking-prohibited premises, such as at pubs and bars, where uncooperative managers have denied entry by NEA's officers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These provisions will deter managers from obstructing or hindering NEA's officers discharging their duties to safeguard public health and reduce abortive enforcement work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, the powers of entry will be exercised judiciously by trained and authorised officers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have earlier set out the restrictions on the exercise of the powers of entry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The new section 4A also does not allow authorised officers to make forcible entry under any circumstances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The powers can only be exercised for the purposes of the Act, namely, to enforce the smoking prohibition.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Authorised officers would only be allowed to take possession of materials related to the suspected offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In practice, we will ensure that only officers directly investigating the case may access the evidence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Similar obstruction provisions and penalties are also found in other laws, such as the Environmental Public Health Act (EPHA) administered by NEA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under EPHA, any person who obstructs or hinders an authorised officer in the performance of his duties under the Act will be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000, and, in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or both.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will regularly review the penalty for breaches to the Act, as suggested by Ms Thanaletchimi.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Taken together, these provisions will serve to enhance NEA's operational effectiveness and efficiency in discharging its responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked whether MCSTs have to pass a by-law to disallow smoking within the compound of private condominiums.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smoking is already prohibited in the common areas of private estates, including the lift lobby, void decks and common function rooms.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, no by-law is required to prohibit smoking in these areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's proposal to restrict the sales volume of cigarettes and increase the tax on tobacco, I will convey her suggestions to my Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Finance colleagues administering the tobacco excise regime for them to consider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Orchard Road NSZ will ensure a clean and healthy environment for shoppers and visitors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have come a long way, and many segments of society support our push for a healthier living environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smoking habits, however, are hard to break, and we must persevere in helping those who are trying their best to quit smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government will persist in our efforts to control access to tobacco products and discourage smoking through a combination of fiscal, regulatory and educational measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, these efforts alone are insufficient without the help of the community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Families and friends should give smokers emotional and psychological support to kick the habit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Orchard Road NSZ represents our commitment to safeguarding the health of the community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I hope smokers will also support our efforts to maintain a conducive environment for all.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Perhaps, we can consider putting up designated smoking points (DSPs), like what we have done in Nee Soon South, because I see that there are more and more smokers who go and use the DSPs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My second question is on smoking in the presence of young children at home.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Sometimes, I see parents smoking in front of children who are very young and crawling on the floor.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Is there anything that we can do to help these young children because they are taking in second-hand smoke every day?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The last question I would like to ask is: how to enforce non-smoking at common areas in condominiums because your officers will not be able to go in?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, we want to ensure that there is high compliance and that the DSAs are appropriately used.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The locations of the DSAs will also be important – how they are designed and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, that is the reason why we are saying that we will implement at the Orchard Road area first.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will look at it before we decide if we will replicate this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding setting up more DSPs, as I have noted earlier, if you are talking about housing estates, one of the issues to us is really that because of the density of housing estates, for instance, and the fact that housing estates are where the schools are, where the homes are, there is a challenge, in fact, with implementing DSAs in this area because you need to look at locations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You do not want to normalise smoking amongst children because DSAs are the areas where people congregate and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And that is why our approach, as of now, is to increase the number of smoking prohibited areas even within our residential estates – sheltered walkways, playgrounds, common corridors, lift landings and lobbies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, there are very few areas like Ms Rahayu Mahzam said, where they can smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of them would be in their homes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I said, we will monitor the outcome of the Orchard Road NSZ before we decide if we will be expanding.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding protection of young children of smokers, we need to strike a balance between forcing our values and norms on the parents, and the parents do have a duty and responsibility to protect their own young.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we all can do, as I have said, is through education, raising awareness, appealing to the smokers, to their families, their friends, their loved ones and the community to inculcate positive social norms, and to ask them to spare a thought for their loved ones – their children and others around them when they smoke, and to smoke in a considerate manner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have called a tender to get a third-party contractor to provide the service.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But these thermal cameras have video analytic capabilities and what they will do is that they will detect any strong heat emitted from the object and then they will be able to capture images of the smoking offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That will enable NEA to use these images to further investigate the alleged offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we will contract the services such that we can deploy the cameras, the services where it is needed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we have called for a tender and we are evaluating the tender.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, this is precisely why we have amended the Act.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, for instance, if a member of the public calls up to say that there is a smoking violation, NEA officers can actually enter.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I want to ask the Senior Minister of State who mentioned that we are expanding, that there will be more areas prohibited for smoking.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And is that because of more areas that are prohibited from smoking and, therefore, many of them have moved back to their homes and smoke and, therefore, cause other externalities to their neighbours and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to enforcement, as I have said, for the Orchard Road NSZ, we will monitor the situation when the NSZ comes into force and then, we will calibrate our enforcement capacity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But actually, over the years, we have increased the number of enforcement officers, because of the expansion in the smoking prohibited places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, realistically, there is a limit as to the number of enforcement officers or manpower we can expand, especially faced with our manpower constraints due to an ageing population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Member is right to say that we would also have to depend on technology.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We cannot be expected to be at every of the 32,000 smoking prohibited places, or to respond to every feedback immediately.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we need the community to help us, including getting the smokers to smoke more considerately and stop smoking if they can.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, in total, the smoking rate has gone down.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And by inference, that would likely mean that there ought not to be more people smoking at home.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, in every case of smoke wafting into a neighbour's house, it is distressful to the person.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: People may also be a lot more sensitive about second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But actually, according to our records, the numbers have not increased.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we have actually seen some decrease in the number of feedback we have received about smoke wafting into a neighbour's house.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I agree that the community plays a great role in this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Are there plans to work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to step up education in schools?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And the second question is how many CVs are there currently and whether there is any target or any plan to train more CVs, because I do not see that this is being actively promoted?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the first question on education, we will continue to work with HPB and MOE on ways to enhance our education outreach to the young, as well as to the population in general.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have no target for CVs, but we need to ensure that we have suitable people who join us as CVs.
